title: Snapshot + replaylet pipeline for safe admin runbook replay
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: When support engineers execute admin runbooks (shortflows/shortpatches) we lack a reliable way to rehearse those steps in a production-like context and to safely re-run a failed remediation. This causes inconsistent remediations, uncertain rollback, and noisy Postmortems.

Goal: Build a pipeline that captures a deterministic snapshot of the operator context (metadata, target cluster/service state, runbook inputs) and produces a replaylet: a self-contained, idempotent execution unit that can be replayed in a sandbox or promoted to live after an automated safety check. The pipeline should integrate with existing runbook-as-task artifacts, preserve provenance, and emit telemetry for success/failure analysis.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Snapshot agent: lightweight collection of context (KV cache references, request IDs, diagnostic artifacts, minimal logs, resource markers) produced at runbook start and after each critical step. Snapshots are immutable and stored in the admin S3 bucket with RBAC.
2) Replaylet builder: compiles snapshot + runbook step graph -> idempotent task bundle. It rewrites non-deterministic steps to guarded variants (dry-run hooks, safety gates) and injects automatic compensating actions (undo tokens where possible).
3) Sandbox replay runtime: a namespaced execution environment (ephemeral k8s ns + mock services or curated fixtures) to validate replaylets. The runtime runs an acceptance suite (smoke checks, permissions validation) before allowing promotion.
4) Promotion & provenance: if sandbox checks pass, a promotion action creates a live-run plan with an attached snapshot reference and changelog entry. All promotions require a 2-step approval for P0/P1 incidents or policy-driven auto-approval for low-risk tickets.

Technical trade-offs considered:
- Full system capture vs minimal context: capturing full memory/VM state is expensive and risky. We deliberately capture a small set of deterministic tokens + resource quiesce points to keep snapshots small and fast.
- Idempotency surface: some runbook steps are inherently non-idempotent (eg. rotate-credentials). We'll pattern-match these and transform them into guarded workflows with compensators. Any step that cannot be made safe will be flagged and blocked from auto-promotion.
- Storage & retention: snapshots stored 90 days by default; retention configurable per project. Sensitive data filtered client-side; KMS encryption enforced.

Instrumentation & observability:
- Emit snapshot.created, replaylet.built, sandbox.run.{start,success,failure}, promotion.{requested,approved,executed} metrics to metrics/redwood.ops.admin-runbook.
- Attach snapshot id to all runbook logs and traces; add a Dashboard (Grafana) showing replay success rate, time-to-build, and blocked promotions by reason.

Security & compliance: snapshots scrub PII/secrets, use envelope encryption (KMS), and require entitlement to read. Security review required for snapshot schema v1 (see security_review_required).

Acceptance criteria:
- A support engineer can take an existing runbook and produce a replaylet in a sandbox in <= 5 minutes for typical shortflows.
- Replaylet runs in sandbox and a suite of automated checks pass for >= 80% of low-risk runbooks in our pilot set.
- Replaylet promotion flow records provenance and requires approval for medium/high risk by default.
- Telemetry emitted and visible on the admin-replay dashboard with basic filtering by project and runbook id.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (prototype): Snapshot agent + replaylet builder POC covering 3 common runbooks (rotate-cert, restart-service, cache-warm).
- Week 2 (sandbox): Sandbox runtime + validate replaylets on pilot staging-only incidents.
- Week 3 (pilot): Opt-in pilot for SRE and Support (policy: low-risk only). Collect metrics and feedback.
- Week 4+: Gradual enablement and policy adjustments, extend to higher-risk flows with compensators.

Open questions / next steps:
- Define the snapshot schema and exact fields to include; coordinate with Security to finalize scrubbing rules.
- Decide promotion approval UX (Slack flow vs Console button). PM/Support preference leans toward Console with Slack notifications.
- Estimate infra cost for sandbox namespaces (we may reuse existing ephemeral cluster pool).

Links to artifacts and references are in 'links' below.
